title: Workshop
description: Settings for the guided workshop panel.

defaultWorkshop.title: Default workshop
defaultWorkshop.description: Directory of the workshop to open when JupyterLab starts and no workshop was open before, relative to the JupyterLab root directory. Leave empty to open nothing.

browseOnStart.title: Browse workshops on start
browseOnStart.description: Open the workshop browser in place of the launcher, with both sidebars collapsed, when JupyterLab starts with no workshop to open or restore. Used by images that offer a choice of workshops.

panelSide.title: Panel side
panelSide.description: Which sidebar the workshop panel starts in. Moving the panel by hand is remembered by JupyterLab's layout, and a workshop layout that names "instructions" for a side overrides this.

workshopsDirectory.title: Workshops directory
workshopsDirectory.description: Directory, relative to the JupyterLab root, into which downloaded workshops are placed.

defaultTrustLevel.title: Default trust level
defaultTrustLevel.description: Trust level selected by default in the trust dialog for workshops without a stored decision.

trustPolicy.title: Trust policy
trustPolicy.description: Administrator overrides, typically set through overrides.json.

forcedLevel.title: Forced trust level
forcedLevel.description: When set, every workshop opens at this level and the trust dialog is not shown.

trustedSources.title: Trusted sources
trustedSources.description: Source key prefixes that open as trusted without asking, such as "git:https://github.com/GrahamDumpleton/" or "local:examples/".

disabledCapabilities.title: Disabled capabilities
disabledCapabilities.description: Capabilities that never run regardless of the trust level.

disabledFeatures.title: Disabled features
disabledFeatures.description: Parts of the extension to remove for a locked-down deployment, typically set through overrides.json. Each key removes every entry point for a feature: panel buttons, browser buttons and sections, launcher cards, palette commands and launch link parameters. "open-directory" and "open-url" leave the workshops of the subscribed collections and the installed ones openable; "collections" and "catalogs" stop learners changing their subscriptions, leaving the settings to say what is subscribed to; "available" hides the Available section of the browser; "install-all" removes the Install all button and Remove all menu item of a collection, leaving single installs.

collections.title: Collections
collections.description: Subscribed collections: published lists of workshops that can be installed, as http(s) URLs of their collection.json files or paths relative to the JupyterLab root. The workshop browser offers every subscribed collection's workshops, and its Collections dialog edits this list.

catalogs.title: Catalogs
catalogs.description: Subscribed catalogs: published lists of collections, as http(s) URLs of their catalog.json files or paths relative to the JupyterLab root. The browser offers their collections to subscribe to.

welcome.title: Welcome message
welcome.description: Path, relative to the JupyterLab root, of a Markdown file shown in a dialog when JupyterLab starts, once per browser for this server; a level-one heading on its first line is the dialog's title. Typically set through overrides.json by a deployment such as a Binder repository, to say what its workshops are for and how to end the session. A welcome launch link parameter names a file to show for that session instead.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: Administrator reporting of progress events, typically set through overrides.json. Events are always written to _workshop/events.jsonl in the workshop directory.

sink.title: Sink URL
sink.description: URL that receives every workshop's events as JSON lines by POST, without asking the learner. Leave empty to report only to sinks the learner opts in to.

identity.title: Identity
identity.description: Whether events carry the JupyterHub user name ("hub") or no identity ("none").
